Physics benchmarks

Measurements and reference cases used in the 17–18 November 2026 review. Each comparison answers one question about accuracy or cost.

Equilibria

On the same finite-pressure D-shape input, VMEX and VMEC++ agreed on rotational transform and force residuals. Warm solves took 0.109 s and 0.046 s on the M4. A native DESC solve reduced its independently evaluated force error from 0.408 on the imported fit to 0.00744. The solvers use different force measures.

VMEC++DESC comparison paperTORUX vacuum reference

Fast particles

ESSOS, SIMPLE and FIRM3D traced the same 32 alpha particles for 1 ms. All three agreed on every QA trajectory’s loss classification. In ARIES-CS, ESSOS and SIMPLE each lost four particles but only three losses were shared. FIRM3D lost three. Recheck those individual orbits before changing tracing defaults.

ESSOS benchmarkSIMPLEFIRM3DCATAPULT GPU studySTELLOPT / BEAMS3D

Neoclassical transport

On a W7-X surface with 11 × 23 angles and 48 pitch modes, four DKX coefficients differed from native MONKES by at most 1.74%. D33 differed by 0.065%. DKX took 2.58 s cold and 0.096 s warm. The MONKES solve took 0.026 s. This monoenergetic comparison covers a smaller problem than a coupled multispecies solve.

Gyrokinetic turbulence

The GKX four-code fixture reports Cyclone heat flux of 6.91 ± 0.19 for GKX and 6.64 ± 0.26 for GX. GS2 and stella have shorter averaging windows. The faster stellarator QA grid shifted flux by 12% against the finer velocity-space reference, so it cannot establish a five-percent result.

GKX, GX, GS2 and stella fixtureGX paperQA resolution study

Edge and duct flow

In DRBX’s one-dimensional Hermes-3 benchmark, matching wall momentum and viscosity reduced the attached-case upstream density difference from 6% to 2.6%. In the LMhdX duct study, friction remained 6.7–10.3% above reference across three magnetic field strengths. Resolve the streamwise grid before using that run to validate turbulent heat transfer.

DRBX / Hermes-3 casesHermes-3 paperDuct DNS reference

Linear solves

On a constrained 2,305-unknown test, SciPy SuperLU and PETSc/MUMPS solved both the forward and transpose equations to roundoff. On the tested PETSc/SuperLU_DIST build, requesting a transpose solve left a relative residual of 0.424. Factoring the transpose explicitly reduced it below 7 × 10⁻¹⁶. Verify the residual before using a backend for gradients.
